results.title: z-head: a segment-quality classifier for robot motion data — architecture, augmentation, results
results.summary: An explainer page for the classifier that decides whether a robot motion segment contains only its labelled action: layer-by-layer architecture with equations (frozen 1D conv autoencoder to one 512-d vector per 0.2 s, no quantization; 6-layer bidirectional transformer, 10.9 M params, conditioned on the claimed action class; a per-step head and a segment head, reject if either crosses 0.5), the four synthetic augmentations and their label rules (all sampled inside one original recording, never spliced across recordings), and what it actually measures. Dirt recall is 87-100% across three eval sets including a locked pre-annotation run on random deployment-pool samples; clean recall is 9-38%, so it cannot yet be used to filter the 28k pool. Includes the purity algebra showing why 90% kept-purity on walk demands 98.5% dirt recall.
results.thumbnailAlt: Architecture data-flow diagram: motion segment to 106-d per-frame kinematic features to a frozen domain-adapted conv autoencoder producing one 512-d vector per 0.2 s, then a 6-layer bidirectional transformer with CLS token and class embedding, ending in a per-step head and a segment head with the 0.5 reject rule.

metrics.label: Dirt recall vs clean recall across three eval sets (the keep side is the failure)

results.title: G1 MotionGPT judge line: z-head architecture, data augmentation and training recipe
results.summary: Design document plus current measurements for the z-head judge: a frozen domain-adapted continuous conv-AE encoder (0.2 s / 512-d vectors, no vector quantization) feeding a trainable 6-layer bidirectional transformer (10.9 M params) with a per-step dirt head and a segment-level head. Rationale: a linear probe reads AUC 0.80 from continuous features but only 0.55-0.67 from VQ codes, and the T5 line never trains on pass/fail, which capped the MotionGPT semantic-alignment route near 0.6 accuracy. Augmentation shifts segment boundaries inside the same recording (no cross-recording splicing) plus cross-class impostors and arm-column pastes. Verdict: dirt recall 87-100% on all three eval sets, but clean recall 9-38% - the model cannot yet be deployed to clean the 28k train pool; a test-then-train rolling loop over the unreviewed pool is running (round-1 walk: acc 0.842, 19 segments).
results.thumbnailAlt: Architecture data-flow diagram: G1 motion segment to per-frame kinematic features to frozen domain-adapted conv-AE encoder to a 512-d vector per 0.2 s, then a 6-layer bidirectional transformer with CLS token and class embedding, ending in a per-step dirt head and a segment-level head with the 0.5 reject rule.

metrics.label: Linear-probe AUC: continuous features vs VQ codes (why the encoder is continuous)

results.title: G1 MotionGPT judge line: part-token backbone (partbert) vs the T5 line on half-B
results.summary: Swapping the judge backbone to a from-scratch bidirectional encoder over upper/lower-body part tokens (register tokens, Muon, bf16), with physically-gated BABEL augmentations (speed/mirror/splice/part-mix, SONIC rollout gate incl. an FK-verified mirror), does not beat the T5 discrete-token line on the untouched half-B exam: best arm 0.670@22% recall is the top of a 5-seed band (median 0.612) vs 0.578@32% for the incumbent; the preregistered criterion (purity>0.578 at recall≥30%) fails on all five arms. The one stable gain: synthetic concurrent-window detection at 0.96–0.98. Ruling: back to the discrete-token default line.

results.title: G1 MotionGPT stage 2: naming the action vs detecting contamination
results.summary: A motion-language model trained natively in G1 joint space (VQ-VAE motion tokenizer + Flan-T5 with the text side frozen) is asked to name the actions inside a VADCompose segment, so that an unexpected second action would flag contamination. Adding VADCompose Cleaned V3 clean segments to the training mix teaches the target vocabulary, but on the fully held-out split discrimination AUC is 0.477 (extra actions named) and 0.526 (nominal-action surprisal) against a 0.615 handcrafted-feature baseline, and contaminated segments have their nominal action named slightly more often than clean ones. A 0.706 AUC on the other split is reported and rejected: 1,248 of its 1,559 clean segments were in training. Two measurement defects that had been scoring correct predictions as wrong are documented and fixed.
results.thumbnailAlt: Two panels: bar chart of nominal-action naming rate on the held-out split, clean 0.324 and dirty 0.370 above a 0.082 majority-class baseline, and three dots for discrimination AUC where the two held-out readouts 0.477 and 0.526 fall below the 0.615 handcrafted baseline while a training-contaminated 0.706 sits above it.

results.title: Clap pool form composition and tracker closure audit (V2 pool, TASK-067)
results.summary: Full-population audit of the 197 V2 clap segments. Reference side: 54.3% are hold-form (hands together for most of the clip; 83 clap-then-hold + 24 held throughout), 45.7% single claps, zero repeated claps — a property inherited from the source data, since the 50 Hz reference is a pure resample of the release with no step that could introduce hand contact. Execution side: the tracker rarely reproduces the reference hand closure — median closest wrist distance 0.142 m executed vs 0.071 m in reference (+6.1 cm gap); only 14.3% of clips reach reference closure within 2 cm, and the gate-passing set (11.5%) is worse than the rejected set (22.9%). Classification thresholds are not yet human-calibrated; a per-clip review queue grouped by form is prepared.

results.title: Rollouts V3 as delivered: gate, executor assignment, and the tracking-quality envelope
results.summary: 50Hz executed-state humanoid trajectories for planner training. Two controllers with complementary measured failure modes split the work: D6 GTrXL self-generates jitter on locomotion (jerk 6.8x/4.4x reference) while SONIC low-passes motion away and runs its arms 80-100 ms late, so kick and walk go to SONIC and the six upper-body actions to D6. Four criteria on joint kinematics keep 1063 of 1392 clips. Because none of them reads world position, this report measures that separately: world-frame limb deviation spans 45x across actions (0.029 to 1.314 m) but collapses to 0.033-0.128 m once the pelvis is aligned — the failure mode is accumulated root drift, only in locomotion, and relative limb motion holds everywhere.
